%s is not a removable card. If it is the: %s is not a removable card. If it is the wrong disk, what is on it is destroyed and cannot be recovered. Check the name and the size once more before you go on.

A different system image (for example a: A different system image (for example a GSI) replaces the andr36oid system. It must be an ARM64 GSI for Android 11 or newer that fits the 2.2 GiB system partition; most newer GSIs are larger. andr36oid features, updates and support do not apply to it.

Android is much heavier on storage than: Android is much heavier on storage than ArkOS and similar Linux firmware. Use a high-quality, fast microSD card for a smooth experience.

Choose the DTB file from your console’s: Choose the DTB file from your console’s original ArkOS, dArkOS or EmuELEC card. It is in the BOOT partition, often named rk3326-r36s-linux.dtb. The flasher turns it into an andr36oid DTB: it copies your console’s screen, buttons, battery and other board details into the andr36oid DTB of the same board family. Your file and the files it replaces are kept in the andr36oid-dtb-backup folder on BOOT.

Custom DTBs must be built specifically f: Custom DTBs must be built specifically for andr36oid. DTBs from other custom firmwares are unlikely to work.

Nobody on the andr36oid team has tested this device tree on real hardware. It can leave the screen black or the buttons dead, and in the worst case put a wrong voltage on part of the board.

Support for experimental device trees is very limited. If something doesn't work:
• Report it only in the clone issue tracker: %s
• Attach all the boot files from a system that works on your console, for example from the SD card it came with: every .dtb file and the other files at the top of its first drive.
• Answer every question in the issue form.
